statement: The coverage probability of a sample-dependent confidence interval $(T_u, T_v)$ is the probability that the interval includes the true parameter of interest $\vartheta$, satisfying $P(T_u \le \vartheta \le T_v) \ge \gamma$ for any allowed parameter $\vartheta$ (where $\gamma$ is the nominal coverage probability), or in statistical prediction, the probability that a prediction interval includes an out-of-sample value of the random variable.

symbols.meaning: lower limit of the confidence interval
upper limit of the confidence interval
nominal coverage probability (confidence coefficient or confidence level)
probability evaluated as long-run frequency over hypothetical repetitions

properties.property: Under long-run frequency evaluation, coverage probability is the fraction of intervals computed from independent hypothetical repetitions under the same data distribution that surround the true parameter value.
properties.why: the probability is interpreted across repeated data collection and analysis procedures following Neyman construction

properties.property: If all assumptions used in deriving a confidence interval are met, the true coverage probability equals the nominal coverage probability, known as probability matching (or predictive probability matching in prediction).
properties.why: the theoretical construction assumptions hold exactly without distortion

properties.property: When the actual coverage probability exceeds the nominal coverage probability, the interval is conservative; when it is strictly less than nominal, the interval is anti-conservative (permissive).
properties.why: unmet assumptions cause true coverage to deviate in either direction from the nominal confidence level

assumptions.assumption: All distributional and modeling assumptions used in deriving the confidence interval hold exactly.
assumptions.breaks_when: Approximations are introduced (such as approximating a discrete distribution with a continuous one) or underlying model assumptions fail.

failure_modes.cause: Model assumptions fail or continuous approximations break down, leading the interval to fail to cover the true parameter at the nominal rate.

failure_modes.signature: True coverage probability fluctuates and rarely equals the nominal confidence level across parameter values
failure_modes.cause: Approximating a discrete distribution by a continuous distribution, such as in the construction of binomial confidence intervals (e.g., Wald intervals).
